note: Banks (1919) recorded only the soldier, and the original itself notes that "this soldier may not belong to K. posticus; if not, it is a new species, and the soldier of K. posticus remains unknown"; the alate of this species was described by Hagen, whose text was not obtained in this round, so this entry has only a soldier section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier: head yellow, mandibles reddish brown with black tips; pronotum pale brown; body dull yellow, legs and antennae pale. Head about twice as long as wide, the sides parallel and hardly convex, broadly rounded posteriorly; the anterior part rather steeply inclined; clypeus subsquare; mandibles shorter than the head width, stout, the teeth as usual; antennae short, hardly as long as the head width, segment 3 not modified; eyes not visible; pronotum more than twice as wide as long, the anterior margin concave, the posterior margin slightly convex, the sides rounded, hardly narrowed posteriorly; head and body with scattered erect hairs of medium length; legs short, the hind femora much swollen. Head length 3 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Banks (1919) examined material from the Botanical Station, Cinchona, Jamaica (collected by Grossbeck on 1924-2-24, A. M. N. H.), taken under the bark of a dead pine. The original notes that this soldier may not be the soldier of this species; if not, it is a new species, and the soldier of K. posticus remains unknown. Alate material comes from St. Thomas, Cuba and Haiti.
